page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a high-capacity server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 144 dedicated vCPUs derived from 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 540 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU, alongside a massive 504 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-144 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, achieving top-tier read and write bandwidths for both cached and uncached large blocks. The server also excels in specialized workloads, showing top-tier capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptographic operations. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50%, though Geekbench single-core scores remain in the top 10%.

Given its high resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized enterprise workloads that can leverage its massive core count and memory bandwidth without requiring local SSDs or GPU acceleration. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token throughput.
